get.description:
Liveness: is this process serving requests?

Unauthenticated, and it does not touch the database: it must not fail for reasons a restart
cannot fix.

Readiness: can this process reach its database?

Pings MongoDB and returns 503 with `DB-CONN-002` if it cannot. Requires the system key.
Report the running API version. Requires the system key; not intended for public consumption.

List Spiele matching the given filters.

Omitting `saison_id` returns the CURRENT season. `saison_phase` accepts `playoffs` as an alias
for "any phase except gruppenphase", and `ausstehend` includes today.

Return one match by its id.

No season is resolved and no status derived: the match carries its own `saison_id`, and
`spiel_status` is a property of a query rather than of a match.

patch.description:
Update one Spiel and resolve the season's bracket.

The payload is written wholesale: an omitted field is overwritten, and every name it carries is
composed by the server. A result can fill or empty the slots below it, each named in
`advanced_to`. `dry_run=true` answers the same and writes nothing.

parameters.name: dry_run

schema.description: Report what this payload would move and destroy, and write nothing
schema.title: Dry Run

parameters.description: Report what this payload would move and destroy, and write nothing

get.description:
List teams for a season.

`in_gruppen=true` returns the four groups keyed A-D, otherwise a plain list; check `format` to
tell them apart. Omitting `saison_id` returns the CURRENT season, and a team not in it is absent.

schema.title: Response Get Teams Api V0 Teams Get

post.description: Create a club. `shorthand` is unique across every club, retired ones included, so a duplicate is a 409.

get.description:
Return one team, with its group and its statistics for a season.

The path names WHICH TEAM; the query names WHICH SEASON'S figures: `gruppe` and `statistik` are
season-scoped. 404 for an id naming no team, and for one with no row that season.

patch.summary: Update a team and fan the rename out
patch.description:
Update a club, then rewrite the name and shorthand its unfinished seasons carry.

The fan-out is not optional: the junction and every match carry a copy of both fields, so
without it a stale name stands indefinitely. A `past` season is left alone -- it is the record
of the name the club was played under.

delete.description:
Retire a club from the league. SOFT: `inactive_since` is stamped and the document stays.

Refused while the club is entered in an `active` or `future` season. Its junction rows are left
alone: the seasons it played still happened.

get.description:
List matchdays for a season, in the order they are played.

That order is the phase in bracket order, then the stored `position`, which is what
`sort_by=natural` means. Omitting `saison_id` returns the CURRENT season.

post.description:
Create a matchday.

The payload carries no `position`: a create APPENDS to its phase, and the `PATCH` is where one
moves. A season whose knockout phase is under way takes no new matchday.

get.description:
Return one matchday by its id.

Its OWN `saison_id` is resolved rather than the current season's, the derived match count needing
that season's rules.

patch.description:
Update a matchday.

No fan-out: matches embed no copy, so a re-dated matchday is picked up on the next read. A phase
change is refused where it would strand fixtures; an EMPTY matchday moves freely. `position` and
`saison_phase` land in one write, a slot another matchday of that phase holds being a 409.

get.description:
List players, normally for one team.

Unlike the other resources, omitting `saison_id` does NOT resolve to the current season here --
callers narrow by `team_id` instead. Only `vorname` is guaranteed present on a player.

post.description:
Create a player -- the person, and nothing else.

They belong to no team until they have a junction row, and no uniqueness rule applies to a name.
The consent record is COMPOSED here rather than taken from the body, so no admin can write one.

get.description:
Return one player -- the person only.

NOT the flattened squad shape the list returns: those fields are season-scoped, and picking a
season here would make the answer depend on a default the caller never asked for.

patch.description: Update a player's name. No fan-out: unlike a team or a venue, it is embedded in no other document.

delete.description: Retire a player. SOFT: it stamps `inactive_since`, and their squad rows are LEFT ALONE.

get.description:
List seasons, optionally filtered by status (`past`, `active`, `future`).

Unlike the other resources, this does NOT default to the current season.

post.description:
Create a season, always `future`.

The id is supplied rather than generated -- it is the string every `saison_id` elsewhere
references, so reusing one comes back 409. Making the season live is a separate step.

get.description: Return the season currently marked active -- what every other endpoint resolves an omitted `saison_id` against.
Return one season by its four-character id; 404 when none carries it, rather than an empty list.

patch.summary: Update a Saison's dates and rules
patch.description:
Update a season's dates and rules. `status` is on no payload.

Editing the points moves every league table on the NEXT READ, standings being derived. What a
finished or drawn season has fixed is refused, as is a rule narrowed below what it holds.

get.description:
List venues.

Deactivated venues are soft-deleted rather than removed, so they stay retrievable for historical
matches. `maps_link` is a Maps search string, not a URL.

post.description: Create a venue. `maps_link` is built server-side from the name and address and must not be submitted.

get.description: Return one venue by its id, deactivated ones included -- a historical match's venue is the case worth answering.

patch.summary: Update a Spielort and fan the change out
patch.description:
Update a venue, then update every Spiel that embeds it.

The fan-out is not optional: without it, match cards keep showing the old name. `mietpreis` is
NOT fanned out -- the rent on a match is what was agreed for that match.

delete.description:
Deactivate a venue. SOFT: it stamps `inactive_since`, and the document stays.

Matches embed a copy, so a hard delete would orphan every historical match that used it. Refused
while an unplayed fixture is still booked here (`REQ-RETIRE-003`).

get.description: List referees; deactivated ones are soft-deleted rather than removed, so historical matches stay resolvable.

post.description: Create a referee. `inactive_since` is set to null here and is not part of the payload.

get.description: Return one referee by their id, deactivated ones included -- a historical match references them by id.

patch.summary: Update a Schiedsrichter and fan the change out
patch.description:
Update a referee, then update the embedded name on every Spiel that uses them.

Only the name. `payment` is NOT propagated: the fee on a match is what was agreed for it.

delete.description: Deactivate a referee. SOFT, for the same reason as venues: matches embed a copy.

get.description:
List Spiele needing an admin's attention, and the bracket faults among them.

Qualifying: cancelled, missing a date, time, venue or referee, past with no result, or a
knockout side holding neither team nor `quelle`. Every season.

get.summary: One Spiel for the admin editor
get.description:
Return one match in the joined shape `GET /spiele/{spiel_id}` serves, under the admin key.

The editor reads here rather than there because it round-trips `ort.mietpreis` and
`schiedsrichter.payment`, which belong to the admin tier.

get.summary: Every team with its season memberships
get.description:
Every team, retired ones included, each with every season membership it holds. Sorted by name.

`GET /teams` cannot answer it: that read is season-scoped with a strict junction join.

post.description: Clear `inactive_since`, restoring a retired club to reads that hide retired ones.

post.summary: Enter a team into a season
post.description:
Enter a team into a season, in a group, under the name the club carries today.

A team with no row here is ABSENT from that season entirely: the join is strict. Refused unless
the club is still in the league, the season is `future`, and the group it names has space.

patch.summary: Change a team's group or record its exit from the season
patch.description:
Change which group a team is in for a season, or record that it has left.

An `austritt` -- a disqualification or a withdrawal -- is how a team leaves a season; there is no
delete. Both fields are required, so an omitted `austritt` is a 422 rather than a team quietly
reinstated.

get.summary: Every Spieler with their squad rows
get.description:
Every player, retired ones included, each with every squad row they hold.

`GET /spieler` cannot answer it at any setting: with a `saison_id` the junction join is strict,
without one a player with no row comes back missing `team_id`.

post.description: Clear `inactive_since`, putting the player back into every read that hides retired ones.

post.summary: Add a Spieler to a squad
post.description:
Put a player in a team's squad for a season.

One row per player per season, enforced by a unique index, so moving a player is a PATCH of
`team_id` rather than a second row. A repeat is a 409, retired rows included. Refused once the
squad holds the season's `max_kadergroesse` members.

patch.description:
Update a player's squad entry for that season.

Changing `team_id` is how a transfer is recorded, and the team it moves TO must have room.
`nummer` stays free TEXT and a DUPLICATE IS PERMITTED
(`fl_backend/app/core/domain.py :: UNENFORCED`): the league fields four keepers on 1.

delete.summary: Remove a Spieler from a squad
delete.description:
Take a player out of a season's squad. SOFT: the row stays.

The row records that this player wore this number in this squad, which stays true after they
leave. `include_inactive=true` is how an admin list gets it back.

post.summary: Put a Spieler back in a squad they left
post.description:
Clear a squad row's `inactive_since`, with the number and position it had.

Where a repeat create is redirected: the row still holds the unique key, and a create reviving
it would overwrite the number and position it carries. Refused where the squad has since filled
up -- a retired row gave its place back, and somebody else may be standing in it.

Make this the active season, moving whichever holds `active` to `past`.

The only path to `status: "active"`. One transaction, so the league never briefly holds no
active season, nor two. The outgoing must be finished, and a `past` target refused.

Exchange the groups of two clubs entered in this season, as one write.

Every Gruppenphase fixture fielding either club has that side rewritten in the same transaction,
so each group stays a round robin. Neither `tore` nor `austritt` moves.
Clear `inactive_since`, putting the venue back into the picker and every default read.
Clear `inactive_since`, putting the referee back into the picker and every default read.

get.description:
List what administrators changed, newest first.

Admin-tier for the obvious reason and one less obvious: a row carries the document a write
replaced, so this read answers with data from every collection at once, public or not.
Confirm the service is answering. The versioned API lives under `/api/v{API_VERSION}`; use `/system/is_live` for a probe.

FLActivateSaisonResponse.title: FLActivateSaisonResponse
FLActivateSaisonResponse.description: The season now active, plus how many were moved off it -- normally exactly one.

FLAktion.title: FLAktion
FLAktion.description:
One recorded write.

A read model, so nothing here refuses a stored value (`docs/backend/spec.md :: I36`): this
collection holds copies of documents from every other one, and a row it cannot serve is a row
nobody can see was recorded.

FLAktor.title: FLAktor
FLAktor.description: Who a write was attributed to. Mirrors `app/core/recording.py :: Actor`.

FLAustritt.title: FLAustritt
FLAustritt.description:
How a team came to be out of one season, why, and from when.

`grund` is FREE TEXT and PUBLIC -- it appears on the team's page, and this league publishes no
disciplinary code an enum could cite.

FLBracketFaultGruppe.title: FLBracketFaultGruppe
FLBracketFaultGruppe.description:
One bracket slot whose `gruppe` reference names a placing no standing will hand it.

`gruppe_too_small` is a typo and the slot is left alone; `tie_unresolved` is a played-out group
the chain cannot separate, so the slot IS emptied.

FLBracketFaultOccupant.title: FLBracketFaultOccupant
FLBracketFaultOccupant.description:
One fixture fielding a team that left the season before the day it is played.

Derived beside the bracket walk rather than inside it, from a fixture's DATE against a junction
record, so no phase is out of its reach. Nothing is emptied: that is a competition decision.

FLBracketFaultQuelle.title: FLBracketFaultQuelle
FLBracketFaultQuelle.description:
One bracket slot whose `spiel` reference names a match that cannot state an outcome.

Both leave the slot as it stands, and neither is reachable through the write path. A cycle is
reported on every fixture it reaches.

FLBracketFaultSpiel.title: FLBracketFaultSpiel
FLBracketFaultSpiel.description:
One fixture whose two references resolve to the SAME club.

It survives the write-path rule, which keys a source by identity, so two DIFFERENT sources
naming one club pass. The fixture keeps its stored sides.

FLBracketFaultSpieltag.title: FLBracketFaultSpieltag
FLBracketFaultSpieltag.description:
A club standing more than once on one Spieltag.

One entry per APPEARANCE, the granularity `fl_backend/app/core/constraints.py :: report_relations`
counts in -- never deduplicated, because which to correct is a competition decision.

FLEinwilligung.title: FLEinwilligung
FLEinwilligung.description:
What this person agreed may be published about them.

Required TOGETHER, as `FLAustritt` is: a scope with no confirmation date is a claim that
somebody consented, and the surface reading this may not tell the two apart.

FLGruppen.title: FLGruppen
FLGruppen.description:
The four groups, always all four, in standing order.

Built by `fl_backend/app/api/teams/services.py :: build_gruppen` alone: the order is the tiebreak
chain, whose head-to-head criterion reads the season's matches.

FLPatchSaisonSpielerPayload.title: FLPatchSaisonSpielerPayload
FLPatchSaisonSpielerPayload.description:
Replaces the squad row WHOLESALE — see `FLPatchSpielerPayload` for why nothing has a default.

`team_id` is editable here: a mid-season transfer is a change to the junction row.

FLPatchSpielDataResponse.title: FLPatchSpielDataResponse
FLPatchSpielDataResponse.description:
What `patch_spiel_data` returns: every fixture it moved, and what that cost.

Both lists report writes the caller did not ask for, each carrying the result it destroyed.

FLPatchSpielerPayload.title: FLPatchSpielerPayload
FLPatchSpielerPayload.description:
Replaces the person's names WHOLESALE.

The handler `$set`s this model's dump, so a field with a default would let a form that forgot it
write that default over a stored value.

FLPostSaisonSpielerPayload.title: FLPostSaisonSpielerPayload
FLPostSaisonSpielerPayload.description:
One player's membership of one team's squad for one season.

Every field is required, including those a squad often does not know: a caller states `null`
rather than omitting, so the answer is theirs and not a default nobody chose.

FLPostSaisonTeamPayload.title: FLPostSaisonTeamPayload
FLPostSaisonTeamPayload.description: One team's membership of one season. `team_id` comes from the path, `saison_id` from here.

FLPostSpielerPayload.title: FLPostSpielerPayload
FLPostSpielerPayload.description: The PERSON. Everything a squad list shows is season-scoped and lives on the junction below.

FLSaisonForfeitErgebnis.title: FLSaisonForfeitErgebnis
FLSaisonForfeitErgebnis.description:
What a fixture is awarded when one side does not appear.

Both sides' goals rather than a margin, composed at `app/api/spiele/services.py :: apply_payload_to_spiel`.
A LEVEL award needs a season with no knockout round (`REQ-RULES-010`).

FLSaisonPhaseSchedule.title: FLSaisonPhaseSchedule
FLSaisonPhaseSchedule.description:
One phase of a season: how many matchdays it takes, and how many matches each holds.

A phase the bracket does not reach is ABSENT rather than present with zeroes, so the list IS the
phases the season plays, in playing order.

FLSaisonSpielerResponse.title: FLSaisonSpielerResponse
FLSaisonSpielerResponse.description: A junction row, which has no read model of its own -- so it is echoed as it was written.

FLSaisonTeamResponse.title: FLSaisonTeamResponse
FLSaisonTeamResponse.description: A junction row, which has no read model of its own -- so it is echoed as it was written.

FLSchiedsrichterWriteResponse.title: FLSchiedsrichterWriteResponse
FLSchiedsrichterWriteResponse.description: Shared by delete and reactivate — both answer with the referee as they now stand.

FLSpielAdvancement.title: FLSpielAdvancement
FLSpielAdvancement.description:
One fixture the bracket resolution rewrote, and the result that rewrite destroyed.

Both voided fields are `None` where a slot merely filled from empty, so "was anything destroyed"
is a null check.

FLSpielElfmeterschiessen.title: FLSpielElfmeterschiessen
FLSpielElfmeterschiessen.description:
The penalty shoot-out that settled a knockout fixture whose goals finished level.

No `sieger`: a stored one could contradict the counts, and the `$expr` barring it is outside the
database validators' ratified scope (`docs/backend/spec.md :: I25`).

FLSpielJoined.title: FLSpielJoined
FLSpielJoined.description:
One fixture as an ENDPOINT serves it: the stored document plus each side's joined season state.

**A subclass, and the direction must not be flipped**: the stored shape is the one a write can
reach, so it stays free of derived fields.

FLSpielOrtFieldPayload.title: FLSpielOrtFieldPayload
FLSpielOrtFieldPayload.description: The venue as the admin PATCH SUBMITS it: which ground, and what this fixture pays for it.

FLSpielQuelleGruppe.title: FLSpielQuelleGruppe
FLSpielQuelleGruppe.description: A slot fed by the group phase: the team finishing `platz` in `gruppe`.

FLSpielQuelleSpiel.title: FLSpielQuelleSpiel
FLSpielQuelleSpiel.description: A slot fed by an earlier fixture: the side that came out of match `spiel_nr` as `ausgang`.

FLSpielReleasedSide.title: FLSpielReleasedSide
FLSpielReleasedSide.description:
One side another fixture gave up so a team can play this Spieltag.

`team_name` rather than an id: the message quoting this has no `spiele` list to join against,
and the rename fan-out keeps the copy it reads fresh.

FLSpielSchiedsrichterFieldPayload.title: FLSpielSchiedsrichterFieldPayload
FLSpielSchiedsrichterFieldPayload.description: The referee as the admin PATCH SUBMITS it; `payment` stays for `mietpreis`' reason.

FLSpielTeamFieldJoined.title: FLSpielTeamFieldJoined
FLSpielTeamFieldJoined.description: One side as a READ serves it, produced only by `build_spiele_pipeline` and never by a write.

FLSpielTeamFieldPayload.title: FLSpielTeamFieldPayload
FLSpielTeamFieldPayload.description:
One side of a fixture as the admin PATCH SUBMITS it.

No name and no shorthand: the season's `saison_teams` row is where a club's name lives, so a copy
a client typed could only disagree with it. The server composes them.

FLSpieleActionRequiredResponse.title: FLSpieleActionRequiredResponse
FLSpieleActionRequiredResponse.description:
The matches needing attention, and why the bracket ones do.

A fault joins its match by `spiel_id`, never `spiel_nr`, which repeats across the seasons this
route spans. `spiele` carries every match a fault names.

FLSpielerMembership.title: FLSpielerMembership
FLSpielerMembership.description:
One squad row as seen from its player.

Carries `inactive_since`, which the team junction does not: a player leaves a squad mid-season,
where a team never leaves a season at all.

FLSpielerMembershipsResponse.title: FLSpielerMembershipsResponse
FLSpielerMembershipsResponse.description: Every player, retired ones included, each with their squad rows. Sorted by name.

FLSpielerSingleResponse.title: FLSpielerSingleResponse
FLSpielerSingleResponse.description:
One player, from `GET /spieler/{spieler_id}`.

The person alone: `FLSpieler`'s squad fields are season-scoped, and inventing a season would make
the answer depend on a default the caller never stated.

FLSpielerWithMemberships.title: FLSpielerWithMemberships
FLSpielerWithMemberships.description:
The person as stored, plus every squad row they hold.

A DIFFERENT question from `FLSpieler`, not a projection: that one is FLATTENED against one
season, so a player in two comes back as two indistinguishable rows.

FLSpielortWriteResponse.title: FLSpielortWriteResponse
FLSpielortWriteResponse.description: Shared by delete and reactivate — both answer with the venue as it now stands.

FLSwapGruppenPayload.title: FLSwapGruppenPayload
FLSwapGruppenPayload.description:
The two clubs a group swap exchanges. Symmetric.

Neither side carries a `gruppe`: reading one from the payload would let a stale form write a
group nobody stands in.

FLSwapGruppenResponse.title: FLSwapGruppenResponse
FLSwapGruppenResponse.description: Both junction rows as the swap left them, plus `rewritten_spiele` -- the second half of the write, reported not assumed.

FLTeamMembership.title: FLTeamMembership
FLTeamMembership.description: One junction row as seen from its club: which season, which group, and the record if any.

FLTeamRecord.title: FLTeamRecord
FLTeamRecord.description:
The club document as it is STORED, and what the write endpoints echo.

The season-scoped fields would mean re-running the team pipeline, whose junction join is strict
-- and a club being created holds no row yet.

FLTeamWithMemberships.title: FLTeamWithMemberships
FLTeamWithMemberships.description:
The stored club document plus every season membership it holds.

A DIFFERENT question from `FLTeam`, not a projection: that one joins strictly against one season,
so a club outside it is absent by design.

FLTeamWriteResponse.title: FLTeamWriteResponse
FLTeamWriteResponse.description: What the retire and reactivate endpoints echo. `FLTeamRecord`, for the reason stated on it.

FLTeamsGroupedResponse.title: FLTeamsGroupedResponse
FLTeamsGroupedResponse.description:
The four groups in standing order, and how many of each advance.

`qualifiers_per_group` rides along rather than being fetched separately, so a page cannot mark a
cutoff drawn from a different season than the table it marks.

FLTeamsMembershipsResponse.title: FLTeamsMembershipsResponse
FLTeamsMembershipsResponse.description: Every club, retired ones included, each with its memberships. Sorted by name.

FLTeamsSingleResponse.title: FLTeamsSingleResponse
FLTeamsSingleResponse.description:
One team, from `GET /teams/{team_id}`.

Not part of `FLTeamsResponse`: that union discriminates the shapes ONE endpoint can return.
